body:
### Summary

When a virtual environment directory contains a `lib` to `usr/lib` symlink, `uv` installs `console_scripts` entry points into `<venv>/usr/bin/<name>` instead of the venv's real scripts directory `<venv>/bin/<name>`. The launcher is *written* to a path relative to `site-packages` that traverses the `lib` symlink. This results in the following error:

```
error: Failed to install: idna-3.19-py3-none-any.whl (idna==3.19)
  Caused by: failed to query metadata of file `<venv>/bin/idna`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

## Reproduction

```bash
V=$(mktemp -d)/venv

uv venv --allow-existing --python python3.12 "$V"
mkdir -p "$V/usr/lib" "$V/usr/bin"
ln -s usr/lib "$V/lib"

# Install any package that ships a console script (idna provides `idna`).
VIRTUAL_ENV="$V" uv pip install idna

ls -l "$V/bin/idna" "$V/usr/bin/idna"
```

I suspect that this issue comes from the fact that after writing the console scripts, `uv` makes it executable and a recent change switched from using the relative path of `site_packages` to using the absolute_path: [ref](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/9a65753e9a8d0e99e7079114d78001311444c718#diff-f2224e4fc2200243c3f25811f8f3ea23cda624fab45a26a09f91c47d77aafdb7)

```rust
                // let path = site_packages.join(entrypoint_relative);
                let path = script.as_path();
                let permissions = fs::metadata(path)?.permissions();
```

### Platform

Ubuntu

### Version

uv 0.12.0

### Python version

Python 3.12
title: uv sync and uv pip install fails for packages with console scripts when the venv contains a `lib` to `usr/lib` symlink
